Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and named Disney as the lead bidder for some of its assets.
Disney's $20 million offer covers a license to certain intellectual property, and rivals can still bid higher.
The app keeps running during the sale.

slides.headline: Character.AI just filed for bankruptcy, and *Disney* wants a piece for $20 million

slides.heading: A *Chapter 11* filing
paras: Character Technologies, the company behind Character.AI, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware on Monday.
The app keeps running during the sale. If no buyer agrees to operate it, the platform will be wound down.

slides.heading: Disney sets *the floor*
paras: Disney is the stalking horse bidder, offering $20 million for a non-exclusive, perpetual license to certain intellectual property, plus transition services. Rivals can still bid higher.
Estimated assets and liabilities are $50 million to $100 million each. The sale could close in late November or early December.

slides.heading: From *$2.7 billion* to this
paras: In 2024, Google paid $2.7 billion to license Character.AI's technology and rehire its co-founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas.

paras.t: Former CEO Karandeep Anand joined Disney as chief technology officer in September. Now Disney is first in line for the assets.

slides.hook: One of the first big AI chatbot hits could soon have a new owner. Follow to see who wins the auction.
